correctness.rationale: Exact reconstruction of equilibrium, Jacobian, characteristic quartic, one neutral conserved-mass eigenvalue, homogeneous cubic Hurwitz inequality, two finite-harmonic Routh signs, and positive shifted coefficients for all q≥9/4 prove the full mode classification. A cubic discriminant proves b0(q)>0 throughout q>0. The actual standalone SymPy certificate validates all symbolic equalities; numerical experiments are not the infinite-mode proof.

originality.rationale: The complete initiating NPZD paper explicitly derives the conservative four-field Jacobian and showcases negative-determinant stationary instability with separated diffusion scales; it does not state or imply the exact rational one-diffusion-contrast, unique oscillatory unstable Neumann harmonic with positive dispersion determinant at all positive wavenumbers. Related published examples of isolated oscillatory modes concern different nonlinear ecological systems, so neither their particular eigenvalue certificates nor outcomes imply this NPZD claim. Earlier NPZD Hopf dynamics do not establish isolated diffusion-driven modes. Actual published-finding corpus semantic queries and accessible own-claim comparisons revealed no same-statement coverage. Unindexed equivalent examples remain a residual risk, so no exhaustive priority certification is asserted. General reaction–diffusion wave-instability conditions of Villar-Sepúlveda and Champneys (2023) were inspected and credited; they do not provide this particular conservative NPZD spectral witness.
residual_risks: Full text of certain semantically related published-finding corpus findings and unindexed specialist papers was not inspected; their indexed claims concern different models, but absolute novelty is not certified.

value.rationale: In a recently analyzed concrete four-compartment plankton ecosystem, diffusion-induced instability can be exclusively oscillatory, isolated to one Neumann harmonic, and invisible to the stationary determinant condition even with only one differing diffusivity. This precise counterexample sharpens model interpretation and contrasts with source examples requiring strongly separated diffusion scales, without claiming a general oscillatory mechanism is new.
